how: Machines that pull carbon dioxide out of the air must push enormous volumes of air past a sorbent, and their big fans are loud and costly to run, which keeps them out of cities. how: Glaucoma blinds slowly as fluid pressure builds inside the eye; drops get forgotten, and drain implants either drain too little or so much the eye goes soft. how: Lab-grown tissue thicker than a few millimetres dies in the middle, because food and oxygen can't seep in fast enough without blood vessels. how: Desert air holds water even when it is far too dry for dew, but most harvesters must heat their sponge to get the water back out, which wastes energy. how: Farms beside canals and streams often sit just a metre or two above the water, so they pay for diesel to lift it. how: Libraries on Earth burn, flood and are forgotten, and a store on the Moon sits in dust under constant bombardment. name: Floating-drop brine dryer

how: Every litre of fresh water made from the sea leaves salty brine that is usually dumped back, harming sea life, and boiling it dry fails because salt crusts over the heaters. how: Many hill villages have a stream but no clean water and no power to run a purifier.
